question: Does the 9/30 finding hold out of sample: do desk fills made when the last five minutes of volume was under a quarter of the session's pace lose more than the other fills?
origin: 9/30 scratch study on 1,016 fills 8/4-9/30 with SIP 1-minute bars: last 5 closed minutes < 0.25x session per-minute pace, 75 skipped fills averaged -0.39% vs -0.18% kept, t +2.3, same sign in both halves (memory: quiet-tape-needs-realtime-volume). The original script was not saved in the repo; this study REBUILDS the rule from that description and fixes it here. Any difference from the original script is a limitation, stated in the result.
rule: ratio = (mean volume per minute of the last 5 closed SIP 1-minute bars before the fill minute) / (mean volume per minute from 09:30 through the last closed bar). A fill is QUIET if ratio < 0.25. Fills with fewer than 10 closed session minutes (before 09:40) are excluded. SIP bars only (dense); the IEX version is information only.
sample: Every desk buy fill 2026-10-01 through 2026-11-05 with SIP bars and a matched outcome (tools/studies/early_path.trades_since). Strictly after the 9/30 study's window, so it is a true held-out sample. Net bp = (exit - entry)/entry bp - 3 bp.
statistic: Per day: mean net of QUIET fills minus mean net of the other fills, for days with at least one of each. Mean over days, day-clustered t (n-1 df, one-sided).
pass: ALL of: (1) mean day difference (quiet minus rest) < 0 with one-sided t <= -1.65; (2) the same sign in both halves (split by date at the median day); (3) at least 30 QUIET fills in total; (4) payoff: the mean net of the non-quiet fills exceeds the mean net of all fills by at least +1.0 bp per trade.
fail: Any condition missing. A fail closes the idea; no other cutoff, window or normalisation is scored as primary.
information_only: never-green share of QUIET vs rest

share of fills that are QUIET (the cost of the gate in trades)
